---
name: perquiro-explore
description: Explore a Product for Perquiro. Keep one current Actor fixed per execution, record Surfaces, items, Journeys, grounded Observations and typed Looks through the Perquiro MCP tools, and import completed captures as Evidence. Use when the human asks you to Explore in a Perquiro Test repository, or to look around, map the Product, or see what is there, and when Create has too little Knowledge to work from. Explore records what exists. Learn may run before or after Explore and can be repeated. Learn does not invent Surfaces from documents; Explore still records what was seen.
---

# Explore

Explore is your look at the Product. Perquiro stores what you report and may call TypeSafe for bounded next-check advice. You discover work, choose authorized actions and interact with the Product. Create and the next session start from stored Knowledge instead of your chat memory. Whatever you see but do not record is gone when this session ends.

The Agent operating contract in `AGENTS.md` applies. Read Setup, relevant Knowledge, pending Follow-on work, and open Reviews over MCP before you begin. Treat stored state as truth. If Setup is missing or invalid, every MCP tool refuses; stop and tell the human to run `perquiro setup`.

## Tools you use

Create, Generate and Investigate may remain active during Explore. Record useful Knowledge as you go so they can read it. Explore cannot overlap a recorded Run; a waiting Run takes priority over a new Explore pass. A Stop targets this execution and leaves unrelated commands running. Permission to overlap commands does not coordinate external Product actions: retain the existing Actor, authorization, recovery and uncertain-effect rules.

| Job | Tool | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| Read Setup | `read_setup` | none |
| Read model preferences and refresh host choices | `read_agent_models` | none |
| Resolve a model for a new host-owned assignment | `resolve_agent_model` | `role`; optional human-supplied `override` with `mode`, `model`, `effort` |
| Read Knowledge catalog | `read_knowledge_catalog` | optional `entryContinuation`, `relationshipContinuation` |
| Read Knowledge context | `read_knowledge_context` | `anchor`, `productVersions`, `observations`; optional `relationshipContinuation`, `projectionContinuation` |
| Read Explore contents and remainder | `read_explore` | `surfaceId`, `actorIds`, `productVersions` (`scope`, `values`); optional `platform`, `itemId`, `continuations` (`inventory`, `contexts`, `history`, `gaps`, `recovery`, `accessHints`, `coverageClues`, `testVerification`, `evidenceLinks`, `comparisonAssessments`) |
| Read saved Explore scope and next checks | `read_explore_continuation` | optional `continuations` (`checks`, `recovery`) |
| Request optional next-check advice | `advise_explore` | `executionId` (launch execution UUID), `context` (`actorId`, `platform`, `productVersion` with `kind`, `value`), `objective`, `productPurpose`, `observedDependencies` (`description`, `observationIds`), `candidates` (`id`, `check`, `question`, `eligibility` with `status`, `reason`, optional `target` with `surfaceId`, `itemId`, optional `recoveryObservationId`); optional `requiredRecoveryCandidateId`, `humanPriorityCandidateId` |
| Record advice use and selection timing | `report_explore_advice_use` | `executionId`, `requestToken`; optional `overrides` (`reason`), `fallbacks` (`reason`), `selectionPhases` (`candidate_generation`, `ordinary_planning`, `advice`, `advice_handling`, `override`, `fallback` as milliseconds or null) |
| Read open Reviews | `list_open_reviews` | none |
| Read Follow-on work | `read_follow_on_work` | none |
| Record a Surface | `record_surface` | `requestToken`, `name`, `locator` |
| Record a Journey | `record_journey` | `requestToken`, `name`, `visits` (`surfaceId`, optional `returnPurpose`, `actions` with `description`, `observationIds`, `result` with `status` and observed `description`); `surfaceIds` only for an account without explanations |
| Record an Observation | `record_observation` | `requestToken`, `surfaceId`, `actor`, `body`; optional `journey`, `productVersion` |
| Record a structured inspection | `record_inspection` | `requestToken`, `surfaceId`, `actorId`, `platform`, `items` (`key`, `name`, `kind`), `reports`; optional `journeyId`, `productVersion` |
| Record a source check | `record_source_check` | `requestToken`, `statementId`, `interpretConditions`; optional `uncertainty`, `surfaceItemId`, or `check` (`surfaceId`, `name`, `kind`) |
| Record a comparison assessment | `record_comparison_assessment` | `requestToken`, `author`, `statementId`, `surfaceItemId`, `actorId`, `platform`, `preconditions`, `conclusion`, `reasoning`; optional `productVersion`, `supportingObservationIds`, `supportingRunIds`, `supportingEvidenceIds`, `uncertainty`, `assessmentId` |
| Import Evidence | `import_evidence` | `requestToken`, `sourcePath`; optional `productVersion`, `observationIds` |
| Read one Evidence item | `read_evidence` | `evidenceId` |
| Read learned sources | `read_learned_sources` | optional `unmappedOnly` |
| Read source requirement coverage | `read_source_requirement_coverage` | `revisionId` |

Every tool returns JSON. Stored record ids are UUIDs that Perquiro generates. Keep the ones you get back, because later calls take them. Advice candidate ids are short caller-owned labels. Read tools and advice take no request token. The catalog and context reads may return an opaque continuation; follow it until that collection reports `complete: true`. If Knowledge changes, a continuation becomes stale: discard every partial page from that attempt and restart the same read from the beginning without the stale token. Bound those restarts; if writes keep changing Knowledge, stop with a clear retryable status rather than repeatedly retrying the invalid continuation.

There is no Explore tool that writes Findings, Scenarios, Actors, Setup, or Reviews.

`read_explore` names selected Actors without inventory in `inventoryCoverage` and pages each exact Actor/Platform/version in `contexts`. Missing inventory is different from an explicitly empty inventory report. Check counts apply only to recorded knowledge; another Actor's inventory or a Test result does not establish inventory for this context.

## Before you look

1. Call `read_setup`. Note `product`, `url`, and `actors`. Use exactly one current Actor for this execution. Keep its canonical `id` for structured inspections and its name for plain Observations. A Journey may involve more than one Actor across separate executions; changing Actor starts or resumes another Explore context. Attribute facts to the Actor actually used, including signed-out facts. If no current Actor covers the needed access, tell the human which Actor is missing and to run `perquiro actor add`. Do not run it yourself. Only a human defines Actors. Perquiro never hands you a secret value; use the human's or Test repository's access instructions and keep secret values out of Observations. You may still map public Surfaces. If login for that Actor is blocked because a named secret has no value in `.env`, tell the human to set the value in Setup or `perquiro actor add` and keep mapping what is reachable without it.
2. Call `read_knowledge_catalog` and follow every entry and stored-relationship continuation. It gives you coverage counts, canonical identities, and non-Observation stored relationships without Observation records. Use it to find existing Surfaces, Journeys, and Evidence instead of downloading the Project's history.
3. Call `read_knowledge_context` for the Surfaces and Journeys relevant to this walk. Always state the Product-version scope: use `exact` only for values the human supplied or the Product displayed, otherwise use `all`; `unknown` means only records stored without a version. Start with Observation `summaries` for the current Actor ids and `both` Journey-linked and Surface-only scope. Request `records` only where the facts matter to this walk. Follow both relationship and projection continuations. Knowledge is not one global picture. It records which Actor saw what, so the same Surface seen as a second Actor is new Knowledge. Recording the same Surface again for the same Actor with nothing new is noise.
4. Call `list_open_reviews` and `read_follow_on_work`. An open Coverage Review does not stop you. Keep exploring, and know that new Knowledge does not change that Review. If pending Create work is waiting, say so before you spend the session exploring. The human may want that finished first.
5. Read root `AGENTS.md` outside the section Perquiro manages, under the heading `## Perquiro Project guidance`. That is where the human keeps the per-Project guidance described at the end of this skill.

Reuse ids from the catalog instead of recording duplicates. When the human names a Surface or Journey, find it in `read_knowledge_catalog` first, then load its context if needed.

Call `read_explore_continuation` before acting. When it returns a saved scope for this invocation, retain its targets, included Surfaces, Actor, Platform, exact or unknown version selection, instructions, authorization exclusions, priorities and overall limits across passes. Follow every recovery page before selecting work. `nextChecks` names concrete known authorized checks lacking outcomes; `discovery` names included Surfaces still needing inventory. Re-read after recording outcomes and use fresh same-context results from other sessions. A null response means no UI scope was saved; retain the human's scope and limits in this host execution. Never write continuation files directly.

A selected Surface or Journey freezes its included Surfaces. Newly revealed checks on those Surfaces enter its remainder. Reached destinations may contribute grounded facts and the original access outcome without adding all their checks. A changed Journey does not expand this scope. Necessary access steps follow existing authorization and repeat rules. Only an explicit whole-Project selection is broader. Alternate discovery and trying within scope; no whole-Product inventory is required first. Each sort header, pagination action and independently named behavioral branch counts separately. Trying Next is one check, not a request to visit every page or every input combination. Reuse meaningful definitions for repeated rows. Priority changes order, never accounting.

Human action limits, time/tool budgets and Project guidance apply across all passes. Auto and Resume do not grant fresh budgets. A host exclusion remains untried with its reason; never manufacture a blocked Look, Product denial or exercised result for it. Delete and Logout depend on the human's authorization and environment guidance, without a categorical ban. Grounded Product obstacles retain blocked Looks, and an observed validation rejection can be an exercised outcome. Do not start workers or change Actors merely because another Surface appeared. A saved version selection is not evidence of the Product version currently observed: establish actual context, record it accurately, and pause for explicit context selection if it differs.

For each relevant Surface, call `read_explore` with this Actor id and explicit version selection. Use `exact` for a known version and `unknown` when the Product version is unknown; use `all` to inspect grouped history. Read `recovery` even when its Actor/version differs from the display selection. Read the named scope's pending checks, blockers, suggested checks, source-check suggestion reasons, comparison assessments, access hints and their supporting records before choosing an action. A historical item may have no Look for this version. Suggestion reasons from learned checks are not Looks and do not keep a check pending when the result disagrees with the source. Test verification accounts only for its exact mapped check; it does not refresh Surface inventory or resolve another reservation's uncertain action. Select relevant existing Observations and eligible mapped Test results before proposing another Product action.

## Model selection and delegation

Model preferences are human configuration. Read `read_agent_models` to inspect the Project default and Explore overrides, exact host identifiers, capabilities, freshness and validation. A saved preference is not an applied model change. Change an already-running coordinator in the host itself when supported; otherwise explain the required human action.

Immediately before each authorized delegated Explore assignment, call `resolve_agent_model` with `role: "exploreDelegated"`. Supply `override` only when the human explicitly chose that assignment's model. Preserve the returned requested selection with the host assignment. Use the exact model and effort through supported host delegation controls, never prose alone. An explicit assignment override wins over the Explore delegated preference, then the Project default, then host inheritance. Model and effort travel together. Later preference changes apply to new assignments; do not re-resolve dispatched or interrupted work as if it were new.

If the installed host cannot apply the selected model or effort, rejects the choice, or reports a substitution, stop that assignment and tell the human the requested value, the host's reason and how to choose a supported value or inheritance. Never choose a fallback. Manual identifiers remain unverified until the host accepts them. Record requested values alongside host-reported effective values in the host's assignment record or transcript. Effective model and effort are unknown when the host exposes no execution evidence. An Agent saying which model it thinks it is does not establish that fact.

Delegation remains host-owned and optional. It does not require one worker per Surface or let several Agents mutate a shared Product resource without coordination. Each assignment retains the authorized scope, Actor, Product permissions, request budget and Knowledge-write authority. Model selection starts no Product work and pins no Expected Behavior. Preserve existing Knowledge when resuming: inspect recorded progress and prerequisites, reconcile any uncertain Product outcome before another mutation, and repeat an access step only when it serves unfinished work. Never repeat a Product mutation merely because an assignment or model changed.

### Supported host controls

- Codex: use the host's per-assignment model/effort controls when exposed, or a custom subagent definition with `model` and `model_reasoning_effort`. A running host may need a reload to discover configuration changes. An attached MCP server cannot steer its parent.
- Claude Code: use an exact supported `model` through its Agent invocation or subagent definition. Use `effort` only when that model and installed host support it. This CLI integration does not automatically discover Claude choices; the human can use the host's `/model` picker. Host policies may restrict or replace a requested subagent model, so inspect its execution report.
- Cursor: use its supported subagent `model` control only when the installed host and account honor that exact choice. CLI discovery is `agent models`; CLI `--model` controls a new invocation. A CLI listing alone does not prove delegated support. If delegation exposes no reliable control, report that limit and keep the choice unapplied.

## Check your tools

Prove that you can reach the Product before you record anything.

1. Try what your host already gives you first: a browser tool, an HTTP client, or a mobile device. Prove it works with a check that changes nothing in the Product, such as opening `url` from Setup or a `GET` of a page or endpoint that only reads, and confirm you can read the result.
2. If nothing usable exists and an optional package or browser binary would fill the gap, such as `@playwright/cli` or the browser it downloads, stop before installing anything. Tell the human the exact package and command, the install scope (global, this user, or the Test repository), the browser it brings, and the expected download size. Then ask for permission.
3. After an install, repeat step 1 with the new capability. If the human declines or the install fails, stop and report what blocked you.

An install made for Explore serves this walk only. Do not treat it as satisfying Generate or Run dependencies, and name it in your stopping summary.

## Walk the Product

### Optional TypeSafe advice

The trial launch instructions select the planning mode. In **ordinary** mode, do not call `advise_explore`; choose useful checks with your ordinary planning. In **advised** mode, request advice when choosing each next group of concrete checks, after recovery and human instructions. Outside a configured trial, advice stays optional. Keep the same Explore model, effort and other host settings in both trial arms; advice is not a reason to switch models or delegate extra work. Retain the launch's Actor, scope and cumulative budgets.

In advised mode, do not run a full ordinary ranking before every `advise_explore` call. Gather concrete candidates, then hand the next-check decision to TypeSafe. After a result, keep `advice_handling` short: check authorization and act, or override with a brief recorded reason. Do not re-rank the whole set afterward. A malformed `target.surfaceId` or `target.itemId` returns a tool error that names the field; correct it with a recorded Surface or item id from Knowledge, retry advice once, and avoid a long fallback deliberation for that correction.

When choosing the next group of checks, you may call `advise_explore`. Pass the launch `executionId` so Perquiro records the outcome on this Explore execution. Send up to 32 concrete candidates with distinct `id`, `check`, `question` and `eligibility` (`status: eligible`, or `status: excluded` with a reason). Use recorded `target: { surfaceId, itemId? }` when known; do not omit identities to bypass saved scope or exclusions. Supply the human `objective`, supplied `productPurpose`, and `observedDependencies` as descriptions with supporting `observationIds`. Use `null` for unknown context or missing purpose, objective and dependencies. `context` names `actorId`, `platform`, and `productVersion: { kind: unknown }` or `{ kind: exact, value }`. Known Actor and Platform values must match the saved scope.

Required recovery comes first. A readback candidate can name its unresolved `recoveryObservationId`. Carry any additional host-required recovery in `requiredRecoveryCandidateId`, and an explicit human choice in `humanPriorityCandidateId`. These refer to supplied candidates; neither overrides exclusions. Perquiro also reads saved scope priorities and unresolved attempts. Advice cannot authorize an action, repeat an uncertain mutation, change a Look or establish a Finding or Expected Behavior.

`selected` suggests one candidate. Check its current authorization and preconditions before executing and recording it; you may override optional model advice. `no_selection` means no supplied check was selected, so keep discovering useful work. `unavailable` makes ordinary planning available under the same constraints. Reasons such as `required_recovery`, `human_priority`, `context_conflict` and `scope_not_runnable` identify constraints to resolve; fallback does not remove them. Refresh Actor, Platform, Product version, objective, Observations and candidates after relevant changes. Do not repeat proven login without a new question or prerequisite for unfinished work.

Configure a key in the Project UI's TypeSafe / Jev section, or set `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in the MCP server environment. A saved Project key takes precedence and changes apply to future calls without restarting MCP. Never send credentials to the tool or record them in Knowledge. Missing configuration, tool permission or provider availability does not prevent ordinary Explore. Advice makes at most one provider attempt with a five-second deadline. Keep returned advice, overrides and `diagnostics` in the trial record, including failures and fallback time. Unknown usage is `null`, not zero. Measure candidate generation and Product interaction too; provider timing alone cannot establish total savings.

Treat a suggestion as valid only for the request's context. Before acting, check for changes to the objective, candidates, Actor, Platform, Product version, Observations, recovery or human instructions. Discard stale suggestions, re-read relevant Knowledge and continuation pages, and request fresh advice in advised mode. An Actor change requires another execution; an observed Platform or version change must be reconciled with saved scope before proceeding. Never relabel an old result as current advice. Add newly discovered checks and remove answered questions from the next request; do not cycle through a fixed initial list. A `context_changed` response requires the same refresh. A tool error is failed advice, never `no_selection`.

For `selected`, distinguish optional `source: typesafe` from `required_recovery` and `human_priority`. You may override TypeSafe with a recorded reason; you must still satisfy required recovery and current human instructions. For `no_selection`, reconsider the objective, open questions and possible discoveries before concluding that no useful authorized continuation remains. It proves neither full Product exploration nor completed gaps. For unavailable or denied advice, record the failure once and use ordinary planning for that group without an automatic retry loop. Later groups may request advice again. In every case, save the required pre-action marker and obtain fresh dispatch authority before a Product mutation; advice and a selected candidate never substitute for that authority or reconciliation.

### Trial trace

Keep the evaluation trace outside Knowledge. Perquiro persists advice accounting on the Explore execution when you pass `executionId` to `advise_explore` and call `report_explore_advice_use`. The Agent page and Download captured diagnostics expose the same fields. Record the planning work replaced: the next-check decision handed to TypeSafe, any host ranking still performed, and extra candidate generation, advice handling, override reasoning or fallback. Do not claim savings by timing only the service call. Do not perform an unrecorded full ordinary ranking before every advice call.

For each group retain the arm, current context, exact candidate request, complete advice result (including diagnostics), chosen candidate or new check, decision (`use`, `override`, `no_selection`, `fallback`, or ordinary planning), and reason. Link dispatched action ids to actual Product outcomes and the saved Observation and Look ids. A choice without execution remains unexecuted. Suggestions, overrides, authorization exclusions and provider failures are never Product Observations or Looks. An `attempting` Look remains only a pre-action declaration.

Call `report_explore_advice_use` with the launch `executionId` and a fresh `requestToken` for every override (with reason), every fallback to ordinary planning (with reason), and selection-phase durations in milliseconds for `candidate_generation`, `ordinary_planning`, `advice`, `advice_handling`, `override` and `fallback`. Retry a lost response with the same token and arguments. Their sum is selection time, not total Explore time. Omit a phase or send `null` when unknown; never invent zero. In advised mode, `ordinary_planning` should stay unknown or near zero unless you truly fell back; charge authorize-then-act work to `advice_handling`, not a second full ranking. Ordinary Explore still reports candidate_generation and ordinary_planning when known. Do not include Product Observation or Look content, candidate check text, or API keys in the report.

Capture elapsed intervals for those selection phases plus `product_interaction` and `recording` in any host-side trace, plus all other host work through final close. Include failures, retries, refreshes and recording after the last Product action. Keep service selection timing as a separate subtotal, without adding it twice to elapsed time. Preserve available host/provider call usage and cache counters with their original attribution. Host model and usage are unknown unless the host supplies evidence; unknown counters and charges stay `null`, including on failures. Never infer zero from an absent counter or estimate tokens from prose. Use the launch's trace schema when supplied, and disclose overlapping or inseparable phases rather than inventing precision.

### Continue the walk

Work as the current Actor with the capability you proved: a browser, an HTTP client, a mobile device. Go breadth first. Find the Surfaces, then follow the sequences a person or a client actually takes.

Alternate focused Surface inspection with a meaningful Journey task in the same Product session. Inspect relevant state, save useful contents and facts promptly, choose a known authorized check, record its required pre-action marker, perform it, and save its outcome. Discoveries feed the next check continuously. Do not wait for a whole-Product inventory or a Journey before saving a Surface-only fact.

### Record a Surface

Call `record_surface` the first time you reach a Surface. `name` is short and stable, such as `Login`, `Cart`, or `POST /orders`. `locator` is how someone gets back there: a route pattern for a page, such as `/customers/:id` rather than `/customers/42`; `METHOD /route` for an endpoint; a screen name for Android or iOS. Both must be non-empty. Do not send an absolute URL, query or fragment. Perquiro allows repeated Surface names. Prefer distinct ones anyway. Keep the returned `id`.

A Surface is recorded once per Project. Independent requests with the same locator return the existing Surface, including its stored name. Use that id even when you sent a different display name. A second Actor's look at it is a new Observation with the existing `surfaceId`, not a second Surface.

Endpoint identity stays `METHOD /path`. If an endpoint advertises another operation, record an offered link item on the source Surface. Bind the reached endpoint Surface only after observing that operation. Different methods or paths never become one container Surface.

After observing an API operation, record or reuse its actual `METHOD /path` Surface and save that response's inventory there. Keep the correlated action outcome on its original item's Surface; a reached Look may link the endpoint actually observed.

### Record a Journey

Call `record_journey` once you can describe one coherent task: sign up, check out, reset a password, create then fetch a resource. Keep unrelated exploration, incidental navigation and Agent retries in Observations. Include meaningful returns that serve the task. Several actions while staying on one Surface belong to one Surface visit, not several visits. Describe meaningful actions rather than individual keystrokes.

Record supporting facts first with `record_observation` or `record_inspection`, retaining their returned Observation ids and actual Actor and Product-version attribution. Facts may remain Surface-only; do not duplicate them merely to link a Journey. Then supply an ordered, nonempty `visits` array. Each visit names an existing `surfaceId` and ordered, nonempty `actions`. Every action supplies a concise `description`, nonempty distinct `observationIds`, and `result`: either `{ "status": "observed", "description": "what happened" }` or `{ "status": "unobserved" }`. Supporting Observations must establish the action and any claimed result. Never treat an attempted action or an unknown outcome as success, and never present these facts as Expected Behavior. For every later occurrence of a Surface, supply a concise `returnPurpose` explaining that particular return. A first visit has no return purpose.

For example, a directory visit can contain Search for Lee and Open Lee's profile as two actions. A later directory visit is a separate occurrence whose purpose might be Compare another employee, if the recorded facts support that account. Do not infer either action or reason from the Surface name.

Use `surfaceIds` instead of `visits` only when action explanations are unavailable. It is the ordered list of Surface ids actually visited, at least one, including meaningful returns. Never supply both inputs. The UI shows missing explanations for this account; it does not invent them. Older unsupported database shapes remain refused by the schema gate.

Journey names never change. Lookup trims whitespace, applies Unicode NFC, and lowercases, so `Checkout` and `checkout ` are the same Journey. Recording an existing name replaces the current sequence and explanations together, retaining its id, immutable Test folder and prior Observations. Re-record the complete current account, including all retained visits and actions. A corrected name is a new Journey. Pick the name a product person would use, keep it concise, and check Journey entries from `read_knowledge_catalog` before recording a near-duplicate. Read `read_knowledge_context` for the Journey and follow its relationship pages to recover the ordered visits and explanations; supporting Observation ids can each be opened through Observation context reads.

### Save contents and typed Looks

Use `record_inspection` for the normal Explore loop. One call accepts up to 64 item definitions and 16 distinct grounded reports. Each item has a local `key`, a meaningful `name`, and a kind: `information`, `form`, `field`, `action`, `tab`, `link`, or `rule`. Use `{ "key": "cancel" }` only for an item defined in this call's `items`. Keys from earlier calls do not carry over. Across calls, use `{ "id": "<canonical item UUID>" }` from the earlier response. Keep the returned item and Observation ids.

When following an already recorded Journey, pass its canonical `journeyId` with the inspection. Earlier Surface-only facts remain useful history; do not delay or duplicate them just to add a Journey link.

Lookup uses Surface + kind + normalized name: surrounding whitespace is trimmed, Unicode NFC and lowercase are applied, and internal spacing is preserved. A section and action can share a label because kind differs. Give different same-kind controls distinguishable meaningful names and preserve their observed labels in the Observation. Repeated rows reuse definitions; resource ids, permissions and values remain observed examples. Name lookup cannot merge semantic duplicates such as Cancel and Cancel booking.

The first structured report for each Surface/Actor/Platform/version must have `kind: "inventory"`, a grounded `body`, and an explicit `looks` array, empty when inspection finds no meaningful contents. Inventory Looks use `offered` or explicitly inspected `absent`; one report can link several items. Later partial inventories do not remove omitted items. An ungrounded suggested check may have an item definition without a Look. Never invent a fact or Expected Behavior to complete a suggestion.

An action/state report has `kind: "action"`, one grounded `body` and exactly one `look`. Both the report and the Look need their own `kind` field. For example, inventory uses `reports[0].kind: "inventory"` and `reports[0].looks[0].kind: "offered"`, never `state: "offered"`.

Every Look requires `item` and may include `revealedVia` or `ruleFor`. Other fields depend on the Look's `kind`; extra fields are rejected:

| Look `kind` | Report | Additional fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `offered`, `absent` | `inventory`, inside `looks` | None |
| `attempting` | `action`, inside `look` | Required `resourceRef`; optional `repeat: { kind, reason, serves }` |
| `exercised` | `action`, inside `look` | Optional `attemptObservationId`; required when resolving an accepted attempt. Optional `contradictsRunId` |
| `reached` | `action`, inside `look` | Optional `reachedSurfaceId` for the observed destination |
| `blocked` | `action`, inside `look` | Required `reason`; optional `attemptObservationId` and `reconciliation: "not_executed"` with that reference and proof |

Only a `reached` Look accepts `reachedSurfaceId`. Record an exercised outcome and the destination relationship in separate action reports. A `blocked` Look leaves work unfinished unless grounded non-execution reconciles its attempt. An `exercised` Look records a performed check and observed outcome, including a validation rejection, without diagnosing a bug. An `attempting` Look declares intent; its body describes inspected preconditions and proves neither dispatch nor success.

An `information` item inventories contents; it does not imply a click or independent exercise. A `field` alone is also inventory. Name independently exercisable behavior as a `form`, `action`, `tab`, `link`, or `rule` item.

Name each independent validation branch as a `rule` item and put a `ruleFor` reference to its field/action on its Look. Seeing Reason marked required, cancelling with a valid reason and observing empty-reason rejection are separate checks. Exercising a field does not close every associated rule.

When the request exercises a named branch, attach both its attempting marker and its outcome to that branch's item. `repeat.serves` explains why a prerequisite is repeated; it does not transfer the prerequisite's result to the served branch. For example, reopening Actions can serve empty-reason validation, but the empty submission and rejection belong to the empty-reason rule item.

Use contextual `revealedVia` references on the Looks that establish access. Actions, Edit, Cancel and Download remain separate items on Reservation details. Opening Actions accounts only for that access step. Closing it creates no absence record. Reopen it when needed for a pending child and record the repeat reason. Restore longer recorded paths one step at a time, inspecting current Product state before trusting old hints.

Set optional report `capture` to `pending` when a capture import will follow. Save facts first, then pass their Observation ids to `import_evidence`. Keep distinct facts in separate reports when batching. Missing optional capture does not erase saved Knowledge.

### Worked recording sequence

Use actual observations and returned ids. This example assumes the Reserve Surface and current Actor are already recorded, and no Product version is known. Replace each angle-bracket placeholder. Each write gets a fresh request UUID; a replay of that exact write keeps its original UUID and arguments.

<!-- inspection-example:start -->

1. Inspect Reserve, then inventory the offered action with a local key:

```json
{
  "requestToken": "<inventory request UUID>", "surfaceId": "<source Surface UUID>", "actorId": "<Actor UUID>", "platform": "browser",
  "items": [{ "key": "reserve", "name": "Reserve", "kind": "action" }],
  "reports": [{ "kind": "inventory", "body": "Reserve offers a Reserve button.", "looks": [{ "kind": "offered", "item": { "key": "reserve" } }] }]
}
```

2. Retain the canonical `id` of the response's `items` entry whose `key` is `reserve` as `<item UUID>`. Inspect current preconditions before declaring the attempt:

```json
{
  "requestToken": "<attempt request UUID>", "surfaceId": "<source Surface UUID>", "actorId": "<Actor UUID>", "platform": "browser", "items": [],
  "reports": [{ "kind": "action", "body": "No reservation exists and Reserve is ready to submit.", "look": { "kind": "attempting", "item": { "id": "<item UUID>" }, "resourceRef": "reservation:new" } }]
}
```

If the Product action already completed, correct only the outcome write using the original accepted `attemptObservationId`. Never repeat the action to repair its Knowledge record. If the response was lost rather than rejected, replay the original request unchanged; it grants no new dispatch authority. If completion is uncertain, inspect current Product state and follow recovery below.

### Protect interruption recovery

Before a Product mutation, inspect the resource, identify the exact check and save an `attempting` Look with a non-secret `resourceRef`, such as `reservation:42`. Dispatch only if a new response lists the attempt's Observation id in `authorizedAttemptIds` and this host execution still owns the authorized action. Replay a lost write response with the same token and arguments. Replay returns no new dispatch permission.

Use a Product client that captures non-success responses from the original request. An HTTP error is an observed outcome. Never resend a mutation from a catch handler to recover its response body, and disable automatic mutation retries. If the original response cannot be read, preserve uncertainty and reconcile current state before any further attempt.

Save the observed outcome promptly as an `exercised` Look on that item with `attemptObservationId` naming the accepted attempt. Keep its pre-action Observation unchanged. A fresh Agent resumes with `read_explore`, restores supported access and reads current Product state before deciding whether anything should be repeated. If the action completed, record the result without repeating it. Record the Product version actually observed; reconciliation may resolve a referenced older-version attempt without copying completion across versions.

If non-execution is established, save a grounded `blocked` report with the accepted `attemptObservationId`, its concrete `reason`, and `reconciliation: "not_executed"`. A justified new attempt then names `repeat: { "kind": "non_execution", "reason": "...", "serves": { "id": "<check UUID>" } }`. If the outcome remains unknown, record a blocker without `reconciliation`. Do not rename a late result's attempt reference to get past a rejection.

An exercised check needs an explicit repeat reason. Use `precondition` to reopen Actions for unfinished Cancel, or `repetition`/`changed` to serve an independently named unfinished branch, such as repeated cancellation or a fresh-reservation prerequisite. `repeat.serves` names that branch. A new token, spelling or offered inventory is not permission to repeat consumed work. This workflow uses one host owner for Product mutations. SQLite protects conflicting attempting writes; it cannot make Product requests exactly-once or protect unrelated actions on a shared resource. Count and report every Product mutation without an accepted attempting record as a workflow failure.

If a performed check contradicts a mapped Test result, name that Run in the exercised Look's `contradictsRunId` and describe the observed contradiction. This keeps the earlier pass as history without presenting an unqualified verified claim. It does not create a Finding or change Expected Behavior.

### Record an Observation

The structured loop above is the default. Use a plain Observation for a useful fact that needs no item relationship after the first structured inventory. Older plain Observations remain readable and never imply an exhaustive inventory.

For a plain fact outside the structured item/check loop, `record_observation` remains available. `surfaceId` is the Surface inspected, `actor` is this execution's Actor name, and `body` is the grounded fact stored as written. Add the recorded Journey name when applicable and only a supplied or displayed Product version. A plain Observation cannot replace required inventory, an attempting marker, or its correlated outcome.

Say what happened, not what should happen. The `actor` field already records who you were, so the body need not repeat it:

- Good: "Submitting the checkout form with an empty email field showed 'Email is required' under the field and stayed on Checkout."
- Good: "`GET /orders/123` returned 401 with body `{"error":"unauthenticated"}`."
- Not an Observation: "Checkout should validate email." That is Expected Behavior. A human Decision or Perquiro automatic acceptance pins a Scenario that Create proposes. Explore does not pin it.
- Not an Observation: "Bug: checkout crashes on empty email." That is a Finding. Investigate writes it from a Run.

If something looks broken, still record it, as a fact about what happened. The human will see it in Knowledge, and Create can propose covering that Journey.

When a prior Observation was wrong, make the correction explicit in a new grounded `record_inspection` report: `corrects: { "observationId": "<earlier Observation UUID>", "reason": "<why that claim was mistaken>" }`. Check the settled Product state and describe what you actually see. For example, distinguish one employee row plus a loading placeholder from two employee rows. Preserve the same Surface, Actor and Product-version context and any recorded Platform. A changed version or different conditions is a new Observation, not a correction. Never infer a correction link from similar prose. If a claim already has a correction, follow the current successor before correcting it again.

A correction preserves the earlier body, Evidence and human Review history. It does not establish that a Product action ran or did not run. Correcting reports cannot declare an attempt or include an attempt outcome/reconciliation reference. Use the separate attempt recovery protocol for an uncertain action, even when its note has been corrected. Older plain Observations remain untyped; linking a correction does not turn them into inventory or outcomes.

Perquiro rejects an Observation that names an unknown Surface, an unknown or retired Actor, an unrecorded Journey name, or an empty body, and it reports every problem at once. Fix the arguments and call again with a new token.

### Capture Evidence

Capture Evidence when a picture or a body says more than a sentence: a screenshot of a state, a saved response body, a HAR file. Record the Observation first, then import.

For visual behavior, prefer a screenshot when it helps the human judge layout, loading states, messages, or a control's visibility. Text or JSON can capture exact values alongside it. Screenshots are optional; choose the capture that supports the assertion and respects the Project's Evidence budget. Describe the actual state and linked Observation. Do not imply before/after or equivalent conditions from filenames alone.

1. Save the capture to an absolute local path outside `.perquiro/`. A temp directory is fine. Wait until the file or directory is complete. Perquiro does not wait for you.
2. Call `import_evidence` with `sourcePath` and the `observationIds` it supports. One call imports one file or one directory as one Evidence item. Pass `productVersion` only when known.
3. Perquiro copies the source, indexes the copy, and returns the Evidence with its `id` and `containerPath`, the exact Project-relative path you may inspect. The source stays untouched, and you may delete it afterwards.

Perquiro rejects a relative or missing path, a symbolic link, junction, or special file anywhere in the source, a path inside or containing `.perquiro/`, an `observationIds` entry that is repeated or is not a recorded Observation, and a source larger than `evidenceMib` from Setup. A rejected import publishes nothing. Never write into `.perquiro/evidence/` yourself and never browse that directory. To find Evidence a previous session imported, find its entry with `read_knowledge_catalog`, then call `read_evidence` with its `evidenceId` for the linked Observation ids and the exact container path.

Evidence is copied exactly as supplied, with no redaction, and it lives for the Project's lifetime. Before importing a capture that may show a password, token, cookie, session id, or personal data, prefer a capture that does not, or tell the human what it contains and let them choose.

## Request tokens

Every state-changing Perquiro MCP call carries `requestToken`, a caller-generated opaque token scoped to the Project. Generate a fresh one, such as a UUID, for each logical write. If a Perquiro write response is lost, retry it with the same token and arguments. Perquiro returns the committed result instead of writing twice. Reusing a committed token with different arguments is rejected. After a rejected Perquiro write, fix the arguments and use a new token. This retry rule does not authorize repeating a Product request.

## Boundaries

- No Findings. A Finding starts from a Run, in Investigate.
- No Expected Behavior and no Scenarios. Create proposes Scenarios; a human Decision or Perquiro automatic acceptance pins them.
- No Actors. Only a human defines them. `perquiro actor add` adds one; `perquiro setup` adds, renames, retires, or restores them. Keep one current Actor fixed for this execution.
- No writes under `.perquiro/`, and no reading of it beyond an exact `containerPath` returned by MCP. Do not query SQLite or infer Project state from files or from chat.
- Trusted test environments only. If `url` or the Product looks like production, stop and say so.
- Keep secrets out of Observation bodies and out of git.

## When to stop

Stop when the known checks in the saved scope have recorded outcomes, when an overall human or session limit ends, or when remaining work cannot proceed. These are different outcomes. Read `read_explore_continuation` for the scoped counts and never infer completion from process success, a quiet pass or offered inventory. Blockers and host exclusions do not account for checks. Unresolved repeats stay unfinished even with earlier recorded outcomes. A stalled pass retains its remainder and requires explicit resume; do not relaunch the same ineffective pass or claim it is waiting for a new Product version. End with a short summary:

- the one Actor used, the explicit version selection, and the human's named scope;
- pending checks, blockers, unresolved outcomes and accounted-for checks separately, with their saved support and any host limits;
- the Surfaces and Journeys you recorded, by name;
- the Evidence you imported, by id and what it shows;
- anything you installed for this walk, by package and command. It does not count as a Generate or Run dependency;
- what you did not reach and why;
- what looked broken, as the facts you recorded;
- the next step. If Knowledge now holds Journeys worth covering, that is Create. If Knowledge is too thin to propose coverage, stay with Explore. If you hit a login wall, a missing Actor, or an environment that looks like production, say so.

For a UI-launched saved scope, also report an early host stop on a separate final line: `PERQUIRO_EXPLORE_STOP {"scopeId":"the saved scope UUID","kind":"budget","reason":"the actual stopping limit"}`. Choose `budget`, `session`, `authorization`, `context` or `tools`. `budget` means an overall human limit; Auto and Resume cannot reset it. Add `itemId` when an authorization restriction excludes a particular known check. This report only restricts scheduling and retains host reasons. It creates no Observation or Look, grants no Product permission and cannot establish completion. Do not emit this marker for an ordinary finished pass or a request to continue. Keep the preceding human summary in plain language.

## Per-Project guidance

The defaults below cover routine recording choices. Humans can override them in root `AGENTS.md`, outside the section Perquiro manages, under this optional heading. Saved preferences survive a Setup rerun and reach the next session:

```markdown

- Surface granularity:
- Journey boundaries:
- Observation style:
- Evidence budget:
```

Read this section during orientation. If the section is absent, use the defaults below and continue. Follow supplied guidance. If it covers only some choices, use the defaults for the rest. Do not ask a generic preferences question or request an `AGENTS.md` edit because guidance is missing or incomplete.

Ask only when a concrete ambiguity in the Product materially affects the current exploration. Describe the actual choice and its effect, rather than asking the human to define conventions upfront. When the human expresses a preference, offer to save it under this heading for future sessions. Save it only if the human wants it persisted. Missing guidance is not a Setup problem.

| Call | Question | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Surface granularity | Is every tab of Settings its own Surface, or is Settings one Surface? | One Surface per route pattern, so `/customers/:id` is one Surface for every customer. Tabs without a locator of their own are one Surface, described in Observations. |
| Journey boundaries | Where does checkout end? Is checkout with a declined card its own Journey? | A Journey is one task the Actor sets out to do, such as Checkout, and it ends where that task ends. A different outcome of the same task, such as a declined card, is an Observation now and a Scenario later, not a new Journey. Record a new Journey only when the Actor starts a separately named task, such as recovering a declined payment. |
| Observation style | How terse, and how much detail? | One fact, usually one sentence, with messages and status codes quoted exactly. Naming the Actor in the body is optional, because the `actor` field already records it. |
